🚀 Meet AstroStrategists! 

We are passionate about aerospace engineering, space exploration, and innovation. For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we aim to create an interactive space mission design game combining science, strategy, and simulation. Think Beyond. Strategise Beyond. Explore Together.
summary:
ASTROSTRATEGISTS is an interactive educational game that introduces players to the process of designing and planning a CubeSat space mission. Developed in response to the Space Mission Design Game challenge, the platform transforms complex aerospace engineering concepts into an engaging, hands-on learning experience.

Players take on the role of mission designers, making decisions across nine spacecraft subsystems: Structure, Electrical Power System (EPS), Propulsion, Communication, Payload, Attitude Determination and Control System (ADCS), On-Board Data Handling (OBDH), Thermal Control, and Launch Vehicle. The game incorporates engineering parameters, subsystem validation, resource monitoring, and 3D spacecraft visualisation to help players understand how individual design choices affect an overall mission.

By combining interactive gameplay with NASA technical resources and real-world mission-design tools, ASTROSTRATEGISTS aims to make space engineering more accessible, encourage critical thinking, and inspire the next generation of space explorers and engineers.
details:
AstroStrategists is an interactive 3D educational game developed to make spacecraft engineering and space mission design more accessible, engaging and understandable. It allows players to experience the journey of becoming a spacecraft engineer by designing, assembling, analysing, launching and operating their own spacecraft through a series of progressively challenging missions.

The game features a continuous campaign consisting of 12 aerospace engineering worlds and 96 sequential missions. Players explore different aspects of spacecraft engineering, including structures and materials, communication systems, Attitude Determination and Control Systems (ADCS), Electrical Power Systems (EPS), thermal control, propulsion, onboard data handling, scientific payloads, deployment mechanisms and orbital sustainability.

Players begin by reviewing a mission's scientific objectives and engineering requirements. They then select a suitable spacecraft platform, such as a CubeSat or small satellite, and enter an interactive 3D engineering workshop. Within the workshop, they can explore different component technologies through visual previews, compare available options and assemble their spacecraft. Each subsystem has its own configuration and verification process, allowing players to identify and resolve engineering issues before progressing to the next stage.

The game incorporates engineering calculations and simplified educational simulations to demonstrate important design considerations, including spacecraft mass, available volume, electrical power generation and consumption, battery capacity, thermal conditions, communication link margins and subsystem compatibility. Players can also use the Auto Fix Critical Issues feature, which identifies critical design problems and applies suitable automatic repairs in exchange for five Engineering Points. Each successful repair generates a report explaining the detected issue, its cause, the changes made and the verification results.

After completing spacecraft integration, players proceed to orbital analysis, where they can explore different orbital configurations, including Low Earth Orbit (LEO), Sun-Synchronous Orbit (SSO), polar, Geostationary Orbit (GEO) and Highly Elliptical Orbit (HEO). They can adjust orbital parameters and observe the resulting trajectory in a 3D simulation. Players then select a compatible launch vehicle and launch approach before completing launch preparation.

One of the game's main features is its interactive 3D launch simulation. Players can observe the countdown, liftoff, ascent, stage separation, orbital insertion and spacecraft deployment. The simulation includes camera controls, playback speed adjustments and simulated flight telemetry. After deployment, players continue into mission operations, where they manage spacecraft power, communicate with ground stations, monitor attitude and thermal conditions, and operate scientific payloads. Finally, they review their mission results and explore end-of-mission and orbital debris mitigation options.

AstroStrategists provides two learning levels: beginner-friendly explanations for users who are new to space technology and advanced engineering information for users who want to explore technical concepts in greater detail. Information icons allow players to access additional explanations when needed without overcrowding the main interface.

The project's main benefit is its ability to connect theoretical aerospace engineering concepts with an interactive spacecraft design experience. Instead of simply reading about spacecraft subsystems, players can explore actual engineering technologies, make design decisions, observe their consequences and understand how different subsystems depend on one another. It encourages engineering thinking, problem-solving, systems integration and awareness of responsible space operations.

The intended impact is to make space engineering education more accessible, particularly for students and beginners who may find traditional technical resources difficult to understand. It also aims to encourage interest in aerospace engineering, satellite technologies, scientific missions and sustainable space exploration.

The project was developed as a browser-based application using Google AI Studio and a modern web development environment. The technology stack includes React, TypeScript and Vite, with Three.js-based 3D visualisation for spacecraft models and orbital environments. Development and testing were carried out using Visual Studio Code and Node.js with npm. The application incorporates interactive interface components, engineering data models, simplified calculations and browser-based state management.

The creative aspect of AstroStrategists lies in combining the progression and rewards of a game with the decision-making process of spacecraft engineering. Its continuous campaign, interactive component-selection workshop, 3D spacecraft assembly, subsystem verification, automatic repair assistance, orbital configuration and launch simulation create a connected learning experience. Rather than treating spacecraft design as a collection of unrelated topics, the game demonstrates how decisions made during the design stage influence launch compatibility, orbital performance, mission operations and end-of-life disposal.

During development, the team considered technical accuracy, accessibility, educational value, visual engagement, engineering compatibility and the complexity of real spacecraft development. Simplified simulations are clearly distinguished from high-fidelity engineering analysis, while technical information is intended to be supported by credible space-agency publications and manufacturer documentation.

AstroStrategists aims to transform the learning of spacecraft engineering from a predominantly theoretical experience into an interactive journey where players can design, launch and operate their own simulated space missions.
